hints: Think about what exothermic really means, forming strong bonds and releasing heat to the surroundings.
Combustion always makes very stable oxides like $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and hydration always forms new ion-dipole attractions, so both release energy.
Remember that dissolving involves both breaking apart a lattice (which costs energy) and hydrating the ions (which releases energy), so check if the overall balance must always be negative.
walkthrough:
**Recall what negative means**

A negative $\Delta H$ means exothermic. Heat is released because more energy is given out when new bonds form than is taken in to break old bonds.

Rule to use:
$$\Delta H \text{ negative} = \text{exothermic, heat released}$$

**Check combustion and hydration**

Combustion is burning in oxygen to form stable products. Bond formation to make $\text{C=O}$ and $\text{O-H}$ always releases lots of energy, so $\Delta H_c$ is always negative.

Hydration is $\text{M}^+(g) + aq \rightarrow \text{M}^+(aq)$. Gaseous ions form ion-dipole bonds to water with no bonds to break first, so energy is always released and $\Delta H_{hyd}$ is always negative.

**Check solution and conclude**

Enthalpy of solution has two parts, endothermic lattice breaking apart plus exothermic hydration of the ions:
$$\Delta H_{sol} = -\Delta H_{latt} + \Sigma \Delta H_{hyd}$$
Because the first step takes in energy, the total can be positive or negative depending on which is larger. So only 1 and 2 are always negative.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes 3 as well as 1 and 2. While combustion and hydration are always exothermic, enthalpy of solution can be endothermic (positive) for many salts like $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ where lattice breaking costs more than hydration releases.
options.B: Correct because only 1 and 2 are always negative. Combustion always forms very stable oxides and releases heat, and hydration always forms attractive ion-water bonds from free gaseous ions with no energy cost first, so both are always exothermic.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes solution (3) but leaves out combustion (1). Solution is not always negative, and combustion definitely is always negative, so this combination cannot be right.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only combustion (1). It correctly identifies combustion as always exothermic but wrongly leaves out hydration (2), which is also always exothermic when gaseous ions are surrounded by water.
